subject: Embeddings + Rerank onboarding: playbook, vector-store choices, migration tasks

To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jane Liao <jane.liao@acmetech.com>
Cc: Acme Tech EngOps <engops@acmetech.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Onboarding: embeddings + rerank migration — initial playbook and asks

Hi team,

Thanks again for choosing Redwood. Attaching a first-draft playbook that outlines the recommended approach for the embeddings migration and rerank evaluation. High-level goals:

- Replace current vector index with Redwood-generated embeddings (dense) and run a rerank layer for the top-K retrievals.
- Backfill historical corpus without affecting live-search latency.
- Produce an eval report (mAP + NDCG) so Acme can validate production parity.

Immediate asks from Acme (please confirm):
1) Dataset size and shard/collection requirements for planning the backfill window.
2) Preferred vector-store(s) to evaluate (we recommend Milvus + a managed offering for the long run).
3) Any compliance constraints for storing embeddings (TTL / PII handling).

Attachments: acme-embeddings-playbook-v1.pdf, mAP-testset-preview.csv (sample eval set).

Plan proposal:
- Week 0: Kickoff & mutual action plan (this week)
- Week 1–2: Shortlist vector-store + small-scale proof-of-concept (10–50k docs)
- Week 3–4: Full backfill (rolling batches) + rerank evals

Dylan/Marissa — can you own the PoC checklist + infra sizing? Jane / EngOps — please confirm target dataset size and any network restrictions for a VPC peering or whitelisted IPs.

Thanks,
Monica
--

- Dataset size: what is the number of documents and average tokens per doc? We'll use this for batching and KV-cache planning.
- SLA target for search latency (p50/p95) during backfill vs steady-state production.
- Do you want the reranker to run synchronously (adds latency but simpler) or asynchronously (rerank worker pipeline)?

-Dylan

Subject: Re: Onboarding: embeddings + rerank migration — initial playbook and asks

Appreciate the clear plan. Quick answers from our side: 

- Corpus: ~2.1M documents (mix of short product snippets and long support articles). Average tokens per doc ~420.
- Desired latency: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 200ms for the search + rerank end-to-end (we can tolerate a brief maintenance window for backfill but prefer rolling updates).
- Reranker: prefer synchronous rerank for first rollout to keep behavior deterministic; we can evaluate async later.
- Compliance: embeddings are ok to store for now; retention policy is 2 years, we will flag any PII before backfill.

We have VPC peering available (our infra team will share CIDR and security group rules). EngOps — will follow up with network info.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if you want to run through the PoC steps live.

Regards,
Jane

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Onboarding: embeddings + rerank migration — initial playbook and asks

Great context — 2.1M docs is helpful. Based on that size and your latency targets, initial recommendations: 

1) Vector store shortlist:
   - Managed Milvus (self-hosted on customer VPC) — good horizontal scale, lower cost at volume.
   - Pinecone managed — simple integration, built-in HA, but cost can grow with dimensionality and replicas.
   - Weaviate (k8s) with Qdrant as an alternative if you want tighter schema control.

2) Backfill approach:
   - Rolling batches of 50k docs, parallel workers (start with 8 workers), keep TTL-friendly segments so warm-up of the index is incremental.
   - Use our streaming ingestion + prefix KV cache to avoid rewarming the whole model cache when serving production traffic.

3) Rerank evals:
   - We'll run a 5-fold cross-eval on the provided testset, report mAP@10 and NDCG@10.
   - Include a set of edge-case queries (long tail) from your logs.
   - Script attached: rerank_eval_script.sh (small harness to run hosted reranker vs local baseline).

4) Infra sizing notes:
   - For 2.1M docs with 1536-dim embeddings: estimate ~60–80GB vector store (depending on quantization) + a couple of 40GB GPU KV caches for rerankers.

Next steps: I can spin up a 50k-doc PoC with Milvus and the Redwood runtime in your VPC next week if EngOps can provide peering + a small test bucket.

Attachment: rerank_eval_script.sh

-Marissa

Thanks everyone — pulling this into a short actionable plan below and proposed owners/timeline. Please reply with any objections or hit accept on the HubSpot task: https://hubspot.example/deal/DEAL-8342

Action plan (milestones):
- Day 0 (this week): Kickoff call. Owner: Monica.
- Day 1–7: PoC (50k docs) in customer VPC — spin up Milvus instance, ingest sample, validate latency. Owner: Marissa (infra), Dylan (ingest scripts).
- Week 2: Expand to 500k rolling backfill, stress test p95 tails. Owner: Dylan.
- Week 3–4: Full backfill orchestration; monitor mem/IO and rerank quality metrics. Owner: Dylan + Marissa.
- Week 5: Final evaluation report (mAP/NDCG) and production cutover checklist. Owner: Monica + Marissa.

Risks / mitigation:
- Network egress/peering delays: EngOps to provide CIDR and whitelists by EOD Wednesday (Nov 4).
- Production latency spikes during backfill: use autoscaled read replicas and rate-limited ingestion windows.

Next call: Monica, can you set a 45-min kickoff for Wed (Nov 4) 10am PT? If that works, I'll post the PoC repo and the ingest script to the Drive link and mark HubSpot task as in-progress.
